LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we shorten words like cannot to can’t?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts
2. use positive and negative statements in sentences

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts

What this means
In this part you learn to form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use positive and negative statements in sentences

What this means
In this part you learn to use positive and negative statements in sentences. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use positive and negative statements in sentences.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use positive and negative statements in sentences. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes to a partner. (skill: use positive and negative statements in sentences)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts.
3. Practise this skill: use positive and negative statements in sentences.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we shorten words like cannot to can’t?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Word Classes means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: form appropriate contracted forms of verbs in varied texts.
5. Be able to: use positive and negative statements in sentences.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
